statement.text:
We say that an infinite simple group G is a monster of the third kind if for
every non-trivial elements a, b, of which at least one is not an involution, there are
infinitely many elements g ∈ G such that ⟨a, bg ⟩ = G. (Compare with V. P. Shunkov’s
definitions in Archive, 6.63, 6.64.) Is it true that every simple quasi-Chernikov group
is a monster of the third kind? This is true for quasi-finite groups (A. I. Sozutov,
Algebra and Logic, 36, no. 5 (1997), 336–348). (We say that a non-σ group is quasi-σ
if all of its proper subgroups have the property σ.)                       A. I. Sozutov
